To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

high frequency stimulation of corticostriatofugal projections induces long-term depression of postsynaptic responses in striatal choline interneurons and that this is associated with a cell-intrinsic increase in the afterhyperpolarizing response of these neurons.

potentiation of NMA receptor-mediated transmission in corticostriatial cholinergic intereneuron (CIN) is a critical step in the induction of a pause in the tonic firing in CINs that is a key component of the reward-related learning.

high frequency stimulation of corticostriatally projecting neurons in the contralateral cerebral cortex induces LTD of excitatory synaptic transmission to striatal cholinigric interneurons (ChIs) and that potentiation of N-Methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-mediated transmission is coupled to the development of an afterhyperpolarizing current that underlies pauses in the tonic firing activity of ChIs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and synaptic mechanisms that underlie the emergence and persistence of pause responses in the tonic activity of striatal choline interneurons (ChIs).
the cellular mechanisms that underlie learning-related pauses in the tonic firing activity of cholinergic inter-neurons of the striatum.

the mechanisms of learning-induced plasticity of corticostriatothalamic circuitry and how these changes are associated with the emergence of pauses in the tonic firing activity of striatal cholinegic interneurons (ChIs) during reward-related learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the potentiation of N-Methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-mediated transmission in CINs may play an important role in the emergence of the pauses in the tonic firing in CINs.

the potentiation of NmdaR mediated synaptic transmission is associated with the emergence of a long-lasting cell-intrinsic after-hyperpolarization (LIAHP) in CIN that contributes to the pause in tonic firing of the CINs.

the potentiation of N-Methyl-D-Aspartate (NMDA)-mediated transmission in cholinergic inter-neurons is associated with the induction of an AHP that underlies the emergence of pause in the tonic firing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
potentiation of NMSA receptors on CINs is associated with the development of an intrinsic AHP that is coupled to reward-related learning.
plasticity of cortical synapses onto CINs can be induced by HFS, and this is associated with an increase of NMDA currents and the AHP.
the emergence of pauses in the tonic firing activity of CINs is associated with the induction of LTD at cortical synapses and the development of a cell-innate AHP.
